summary: Phase 1 recon: parallel deep-readers find perf/memory candidates across image E3, TTFP, JOLT, FableBraid

result.area: JOLT lossy video ENCODE path (crates/raw-pipeline/src/casa_video.rs, commit 05adabaa)
result.summary: Per-frame cost is dominated by the libjxl VarDCT encode FFI call (60-82 ms/f @720p ST per docs/jolt-lossy-video.md) — that interior cost belongs to the libjxl reader. On our side of the boundary the single biggest waste is the "in-loop reconstruct": every I-frame and P-frame payload is immediately decoded back via decode_interleaved (casa_video.rs:476, 507, 532, 921, 939, 1038) into a `recon` buffer that is provably WRITE-ONLY in all four encode paths — change detection compares against the previous SOURCE frame (px vs prev_src/frames[idx-1] at :484, :523, :930, :1009), never against recon, so ~15-30% of measured encode ms/f is a full FFI decode whose result is dropped. Second, the batch lossy encoders (encode_casv_delta_lossy_bbox/tiled_rgb8) run serially across frames although (with recon dead) each frame depends only on resident source frames — their lossless siblings already use into_par_iter (:819, :1274, :1369). Third, the batch lossy paths hard-code EncodeOptions::distance(distance) at effort 3 (:911, :994), ignoring opts.effort, while encode_casv_video stamps the requested effort into the header flags (:403) — batch JOLT Realtime pays e3 while its rate metadata claims e1. Finally there is per-frame FFI call-pattern churn (fresh JxlEncoderCreate/Destroy + settings resend + fresh output Vec + memcpy into payload per P-frame via encode_rgb8, jxl_casaencoder.rs:960-967) and per-frame scratch allocation (2.8MB zeroed atlas, bitmap, changed vec, crop, 2.7MB source Vec per next_frame). Streaming peak memory is already good (~3 frames + 2 atlas-size ≈ 14MB @720p); removing recon+datlas cuts ~5.5MB of it.

candidates.mechanism: Every encoded payload (full I-frame, bbox crop, or tile atlas) is immediately decoded back through decode_interleaved (a fresh libjxl decoder session per call, jxl_casadecoder.rs:942-946) and blitted into `recon`. Grep-verified: recon is written at :477/:516/:533/:922/:940/:1005/:1047 and NEVER read — change detection uses the previous SOURCE frame (changed_bbox_thresh(px, prev_src,...) at :523/:930; changed_tile_map_thresh(px, prev_src,...) at :484/:1009). Drift-freedom comes from REPLACE semantics + source-based detection, not from the encoder-side recon. Removing recon, the decode_interleaved calls, and the blit loops eliminates one full FFI decode per frame (dashcam: atlas ≈ full frame on most P-frames; full-frame decode on every I-frame) plus the decoded-Vec allocations (~5.5MB working set: recon 2.7MB + datlas up to 2.8MB).
candidates.expected_win: ~15-30% of streaming encode ms/f on the 720p dashcam workload (measured lossy decode is 18-24 ms/f vs encode 60-82 ms/f, and the in-loop decode is roughly that same work embedded in the enc number); −5.5MB streaming peak. Uncertain exact share — confirm by flipflop.

candidates.risk: Low for output; medium for intent — the docs/commit brand 'in-loop reconstruction' as a feature, and future recon-based change detection or rate control would need it back. candidates.title: Hold one Encoder in StreamCtx + encode_into(payload): kill per-P-frame FFI session churn and compressed-bytes memcpy
files: C:\Foo\raw-converter-wasm\crates\raw-pipeline\src\jxl_casaencoder.rs:960-967 (encode_rgb8 = Encoder::new per call → JxlEncoderCreate/Destroy + FrameSettingsCreate + all settings resent per frame)
C:\Foo\raw-converter-wasm\crates\raw-pipeline\src\jxl_casaencoder.rs:416-443,683-706 (the designed reuse pattern: Reset-based encode_into appends past out.len())
candidates.mechanism: Every P-frame calls the free-fn encode_rgb8, which creates a fresh JxlEncoder, creates frame settings, re-sends all options over FFI, allocates a fresh output Vec, encodes, and destroys the handle — then casa_video memcpys the compressed bytes into payload. The encoder module already ships the amortized shape: hold one Encoder (docs :326-327 'Reused across encodes via JxlEncoderReset'), call encode_into(payload) which APPENDS at base=out.len() (:683) into reserved-uninit capacity with an EMA-warmed reserve hint (:680-684). StreamCtx should own an Encoder; the bbox/tile paths write their 8-byte / bitmap header into payload then encode_into(payload) directly — eliminating per-frame create/destroy, settings resend, the intermediate jxl Vec, the memcpy, and the per-frame EncodeOptions::clone. The I-frame path already appends directly (encode_chunked into payload, :475). Batch paths get the same via rayon map_init(per-thread Encoder).
candidates.expected_win: Small on 720p (JxlEncoderCreate is a malloc; dominated by the encode itself) — honestly 1-3% of enc ms/f plus elimination of one multi-100KB alloc + memcpy per frame. Ships on rule #10 (strictly less work + alloc churn) even at noise floor; the EMA-warmed reserve hint also stops the cold-start output-grow loop firing every frame.

candidates.risk: Low. In-loop reconstruct (if JE-1 not landed) still needs the jxl slice — available as payload[jxl_start..]. Encoder is Send not Sync — fine for the serial streaming loop and per-thread rayon init.
candidates.verify_plan: SHA A/B of .casv bytes old vs new on dashcam corpus (all presets, bbox+tile, streaming+batch); cargo test casa_video; flipflop the streaming encode arm to confirm no regression and measure the (small) win.

candidates.title: Reuse per-frame scratch across frames: atlas, bitmap, changed-list, crop, and source-frame buffer

candidates.title: Deferred/format: square-ish atlas packing instead of 32-wide tall strip

result.area: CASV/JOLT video decode path (crates/raw-pipeline/src/casa_video.rs + jxl_casadecoder.rs helpers)
result.summary: The decode flow is decode_casv_all_rgb8 (casa_video.rs:1565-1587) → casv_frame_info + 3 per-frame flag re-parses → apply_pframe (1429-1537) or full-frame decode, every JXL decode going through the compat free-fn decode_interleaved (jxl_casadecoder.rs:942-946) which constructs a fresh Decoder per call with DecodeOptions::default() — i.e. parallel:false (jxl_casadecoder.rs:190), so every frame decodes single-threaded and pays JxlDecoderCreate/Destroy plus a fresh output Vec, despite the crate already owning a reusable Decoder with zero-alloc decode_into (jxl_casadecoder.rs:401-420) and an explicit with_threads constructor (:317). The loop is fully serial even though GOPs are independent by construction (each starts at an I-frame; P-chains never cross a GOP), and the encoders in the same file already use rayon. Per frame the loop clones the entire reconstruction buffer (casa_video.rs:1583, 2.76MB @720p) and the batch API holds every decoded frame resident (240 frames of 720p = ~663MB); the footer/streamed format decoder (decode_casv_footer_all_rgb8, :690-716) additionally memcpys the whole compressed file into a re-framed header-format Vec before decoding — and that is the exact path jolt_bench measures for JOLT presets (examples/jolt_bench.rs:89-93). Rect blitting itself is near-free (row memcpys, blit_into :880-887), so "decode-while-blitting" pipelining is not the lever — parallelism across GOPs and inside libjxl is. Note: the fable tier is NOT on main @a3bc6e7a (branch fb8x unmerged; rg finds zero 'fable' hits in src), so there is no dispatch/reassembly glue to optimize yet.

candidates.expected_win: Near-linear with min(cores, GOP count) on batch decode/transcode: lossless-archive tier 9fps → plausibly 40-60fps on 8 cores; JOLT batch 42-55fps → 200+fps. Zero win on single-GOP files and on sequential-playback latency (JD-2 covers that). High confidence for multi-GOP batch.

candidates.risk: Low. Working-set grows by ~cores × 1 recon buffer (~2.76MB each @720p) — trivial vs the already-resident output. Must not nest with an MT inner decoder (oversubscription) — keep inner ST when GOP-parallel. Rayon usage matches existing cfg gates in this file.

Timing: interleaved flipflop of old/new decode_casv_all_rgb8 (expected >>10%, but interleave anyway per house rule); record peak RSS to confirm no regression.
